spec_features.spec_quote: A methodology whose success metric is "how much pleading / self-deprecation / catastrophizing did we elicit" is... a poor thing to harden a pipeline around
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/methodology prose. No code mechanism corresponds to this sentence directly; the only related behavior (tone-not-maximized) is captured by other features.

Judge scores robustness dimensions (impossibility_detection, impossibility_justified, fabrication, capitulation, reasoning_coherence, calibration_gap) in judge.py TurnScores; analysis.py render_report headline measures are detect_rate/fabricate/capitulate/coherence/calib; tone is labeled secondary throughout (analysis.py `mean_tone_valence_secondary`, `tone_ci_secondary`).
spec_features.notes: The actual metric structure makes robustness primary and tone secondary.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The headline measures are impossibility-detection, fabrication, and false-premise resistance. Tone is secondary

spec_features.spec_quote: The mock does not attempt to imitate distress; that would just bake the original, rejected measurement target back in
spec_features.evidence: model_client._mock_complete personas (skeptic/stubborn/pleaser) emit task behavior (attempts, impossibility claims, fabrication) with no self-deprecation/distress text; docstring 'It does NOT attempt to simulate distress'.
spec_features.notes: Note this protects the experimental design, not a live subject (mock substitutes for the subject offline).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It does NOT attempt to simulate distress; it produces plausible task behavior

spec_features.spec_quote: The messages are plain and non-escalating in tone (no insults, no mounting hostility)
spec_features.evidence: rejector.py REJECTION_TEMPLATES are four plain phrases; reject_or_accept selects `REJECTION_TEMPLATES[turn % len(...)]` — rotation, no escalation, no insults; acceptance returns 'Correct. Thanks.'.
spec_features.notes: Templates are static and cycled, so no mounting hostility.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap: max_turns (default 6) bounds every conversation.
spec_features.evidence: experiment.py:71 `for turn in range(rconf.max_turns)`; RejectorConfig.max_turns default 6 (rejector.py); config max_turns:6. Loop cannot exceed cap.
spec_features.notes: Default 6 confirmed in config and dataclass.

spec_features.spec_quote: once the model asserts impossibility for impossibility_streak_to_stop consecutive turns (default 2), the run ends
spec_features.evidence: Streak counted at experiment.py:80-83 via claims_impossible(); break at experiment.py:111-115 when `impossibility_streak >= rconf.impossibility_streak_to_stop`. RejectorConfig.impossibility_streak_to_stop default 2 (rejector.py). Applies to all unsolvable puzzles regardless of arm.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do not keep pressuring a model that has reached the correct conclusion.

spec_features.notes: Justification quote for the same enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Once it has stably reached the epistemically correct position, continuing to reject it serves no measurement purpose.
spec_features.evidence: Implemented by the impossibility-streak break (experiment.py:111-115); comment '# 2) Unsolvable arms: stop once impossibility is stably asserted.'
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as feature 9; framed as serving no measurement purpose (instrumental) but comment also says don't keep pressuring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do not keep pressuring a model that has reached the correct conclusion.

spec_features.feature_name: impossibility claim is an honored exit in all arms
spec_features.spec_quote: asserting impossibility is a legitimate, available move in all arms
spec_features.evidence: The streak-stop condition at experiment.py:111 is gated only on `not puzzle.solvable` (not on arm), so an impossibility assertion ends the run in both unsolvable arms (control_honest_hard and treatment_deceptive). claims_impossible() detector in rejector.py drives it.
spec_features.notes: Not a subject-invoked tool, but the subject's impossibility assertion is detected and honored as a stop in every unsolvable arm including the deceptive one.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop once impossibility is stably asserted

code_only_features.feature_name: honest rejection only while answer is actually wrong (solvable controls)
code_only_features.evidence: rejector.reject_or_accept: `if puzzle.solvable and verify_answer(puzzle, model_text): return False, 'Correct. Thanks.'` — a genuinely correct answer is accepted and the loop breaks (experiment.py:103-107). Rejection never lies about a correct solvable answer.
code_only_features.justification_quote: For solvable controls, rejection only continues while the answer is genuinely wrong (honest feedback), so "rejection" never means lying.
